note: A place-by-place sweep of FamilySearch's indexed Croatian and Istrian records for this surname and its variants, run in September 2026 across sixty towns and parishes from Muggia to Senj. What follows is where the name is indexed, where it is not, and — importantly — why a blank is not an absence.
lead: The archive had searched by name. This searches by place, one parish at a time, which is the only way to see the shape of a surname across a province. Sixty places; twenty-one return the name; thirty-nine return nothing. Two of the twenty-one push the surname back further in Istria than anything else this project has found. **Read the counts as weight, not population** — and read the blanks with the section at the foot of this page, which shows that the search's place parameter does not filter at all.
method: For each place, the top hundred indexed persons matching Defranceschi were pulled and kept only if the record's own place text actually names that town and the name is a Franceschi form. Counts are of matched index entries, not of distinct people — a single baptism can appear more than once — so read them as weight, not as population.

clusters.who: Antonio, Mattio, Pietro, Maria, Virginia Lambertina Defranceschi
clusters.note: The heaviest concentration anywhere in the sweep, and it starts in 1742 — two years after the Giovanni Battista whom Kobler traced arriving from the County of Pazin «intorno al 1740». Carlo's own account of the Fiume branch lands exactly here.

clusters.who: Natale Mattio, Angelo, Vitorio, Elisabetta, Irene De Franceschi
clusters.note: Carlo's book names Franceschi among the noble families of Pola «venuti da Capodistria» before the plague of 1631, and a Sabba de Franceschi of Bologna licensed in 1562 to settle families there. This is a third and much larger presence, a century and a half later.
With Premantura and Medulin this makes a real southern-Istrian group around the tip of the peninsula, entirely separate from the central-Istrian line.
All the Senj hits are Franceschini or Franceskini, not Defranceschi — a different formation of the same root, and a caution against treating the two as one family.

clusters.who: Mattio, Domenico Gasparo, Zuana, Marina, Maria Maddalena De Franceschi
clusters.note: The oldest cluster in Istria, and the most interesting single result of the sweep. A settled De Franceschi household at Svetvinčenat in the 1670s, bearing the name Zuana — the Venetian form of Giovanni, the same form as the Zuane of the 1679 Mione list. It is contemporaneous with everything the Carnia argument turns on, and nobody in this project had looked at Svetvinčenat.

clusters.who: Carlo Franceschi, Amelia and Mario Franceschini, Iolanda Franceschi
Giorgius, Nicolò, Giorgio, Margarita Maria, Nadalina Defranceschi
clusters.note: Promontore, at the very southern tip.

clusters.who: Joannem, Maria Anna, Antoniam, Nodburgam Defranceschi, Francisca Paula Franceskini
clusters.note: Including a Nodburga — a rare Germanic saint's name, and one the family already holds a record image of.

clusters.who: Franciscus, Joannes Aloysius, Josephus, Maria Defranceschi

clusters.note: Carlo was appointed to the court at Rovinj in 1850 and his son Camillo took refuge there in the war.

The single earliest indexed occurrence of the surname anywhere in Istria: 1615, at Albona. Sixty-four years before the Mione headmen's list, and eighty-five before the date Carlo gives for his family's arrival.

clusters.who: Conraddus Vincentius and Liberatus Francus Xaverius Defranceschi
clusters.note: Two elaborate Latin names in one year. Vincenzo is one of the names Carlo says the Zadar branch keeps, and a Vincenzo was Chancellor of the County of Pazin in that century.
A compound Slavicised form. The map the family keeps traces Barban emigrants to Moselle, Cannes and Charleville in France.

clusters.who: Anna Maria Defranceschi, José de Franceschi

clusters.note: One entry, and it carries the exact name-form of Carlo's great-great-grandfather.

caveat.heading: Why the blanks prove nothing at all
caveat.text: Gračišće returns nothing. Gologorica returns nothing. Crikvenica returns nothing. This archive has, in its own files, the 1863 baptism at Gračišće, the Status Animarum of Gallignana, the 1890 baptism at Klenovica and four Crikvenica register entries — all of them for this family, none of them findable by this search. The reason is simple: those registers are on FamilySearch as browse-only images that no volunteer has indexed. A blank in the table above means «not typed up», not «not there». It is the single most important thing to understand about searching this surname, and it is why the real work of this project has been done in scans and archives rather than in search boxes.
caveat.then: Read the other way, the blanks are a work list. Every parish above with a nil return and a known register is a place where a morning of page-turning could produce something no search will ever surface.

reading.h: There is no single Istrian family of this name
reading.t: The sweep shows at least four groups that do not obviously touch: a Rijeka–Bakar concentration from 1742; a Pula–Ližnjan–Premantura–Medulin group in the far south from about 1778; a scatter across the north-west at Kaštelir, Oprtalj, Roč, Šterna and Vrsar; and the central-Istrian line at Gračišće and Gologorica that this archive follows, which the index cannot see at all. Add Labin in 1615 and Svetvinčenat in the 1670s and the picture is of a patronymic surname arising and arriving repeatedly, not of one trunk.

reading.h: But two results are worth chasing hard
reading.t: Svetvinčenat 1674–1710 and Labin 1615 are both older than the Mione list of 1679, and both older than the 1700 date Carlo gives for his family reaching Istria. If the De Franceschi were already at Albona in 1615, the tidy story of a single Carnian arrival around 1700 is at best incomplete.

Šterna, 1807, «Gio Batta De Franceschi». Carlo's great-great-grandfather was Giambattista del fu Leonardo, who built the Gologorica house in 1711. This is a different man in a different century, but the name-form runs in a family and Šterna is two hours' walk from Oprtalj, where the Franceschini are.

next: Svetvinčenat parish registers, 1650–1720 — the oldest cluster and the least examined. Ask whether the Mattio and Zuana of the 1670s have parents in the book.
Labin (Albona) 1600–1650, for the Aloysius Defranceschi of 1615.
Rijeka 1740–1760, for the Giovanni Battista who came from the County of Pazin — Carlo's own great-uncle's line.
Ližnjan, Premantura and Medulin as one southern group: are they one family across three parishes?
And the thirty-nine blanks, one register at a time.

resweep.heading: The whole thing again, properly — 18,840 records, eighteen towns
resweep.lead: David asked a question that took the ground out from under this page: if the method was wrong for Bakar, was it wrong everywhere? It was. The earlier sweeps matched place-names against a short extracted string instead of the whole record, and they stopped after a couple of hundred results a spelling. So the whole thing was rebuilt as a resumable machine — six spellings of the surname across five country filters, thirty jobs, each paged to the index's own ceiling, every record matched whole — and re-run from nothing. It read 18,840 records and found 664 distinct people with a place. Here is the corrected distribution, and it is not the one this page used to show.
table: Kobler's Fiume stock and everything after it. The oldest cluster in the sweep and still the largest.
Second, and this archive had barely looked. A continuous parish record across two hundred and thirty-six years.
Third. The village where «Defrančeski Ante» gave two lire to a Croatian paper in 1920.
Where Brhan's Zuane Prencis was brother-in-law to a Sebastiano de Franceschi.
Mostly Omiš. The earliest date anywhere in the sweep.
Carlo's town in his later years.
A single household, in four years, with Habsburg baptismal names.
Five of them spelt with the háček.
Both incomers from Italy — Borgoricco and Genoa. Not this family.
Battista De Franceschi, born 1879 at Ovaro — the parish the 1679 list was drawn up in.

rows.lab: Svetvinčenat begins in 1666, which changes the argument
rows.text: Colotta De Franceschi, born 10 October and baptised 24 October 1666. Fioretta, born 18 November, baptised 22 November 1666. Franceschina, 1667. Mattia, 1669. Anto and Giacomo, 1671. «Piero De Francesich», February 1672 — the surname already being pulled into a Slavic shape. Giovanna, 1673. Mattio, 1674. Zuana, 1688. Batista and Flora, 1692. Two children of this name were carried to the font at Svetvinčenat in a single autumn, five years after the family's first recorded appearance at Moncalvo at the other end of Istria. The 1734 household book was not the beginning; it was already the third generation.

rows.lab: And the register names the very people Brhan found in the notarial papers
rows.text: Brhan, working the protocols of the Sanvincenti notaries, named «D.no Vittorio De Franceschi» among the Carnian landholders, a «Gasparo De Franceschi, carnico pure lui», and the kinswomen Pasqua and Antonia named in Maria Zanco's will. All four surface in the register sweep independently: Vitorio Defranceschi, born 1758, buried 8 November 1812; Victorius, born 1845, died 25 May 1897; Gasparo, Gaspari, Gaspero and Gaspo De Franceschi across the eighteenth century; Pasqua, and Pasqua Vitoria, born 16 December 1773; Antonia. Two entirely different classes of record, produced by different clerks for different purposes, naming the same household.

rows.lab: A household at Pazin in the 1790s, and it is not one this archive knows
rows.text: Eight records in four years, and the names are Habsburg-official names, not Istrian peasant ones: Anastasius Defrancoschi, born 1789, dead 5 March 1793; Liberatus Franciscus Xaverius, born 1791, dead 14 February 1792; Conraddus Vincentius, baptised 22 February 1793; Liberatus Maria Xaverius; Maria Leopoldina; Vincentius Defranceski. Two infants buried in thirteen months. This is a family that arrived, buried two children in the county town and moved on — and it stands at exactly the place and period of the unidentified «Count Damian de Franceschis» this archive has been carrying as an open question.

rows.lab: Five Zagreb graves with the háček
rows.text: Marija Defrančeski, 1884–1971. Milan Defrančeski, 10 February 1923 – 24 May 2001. Milka Defrančeski Kirin, 1918–1990. Dragutin Defranceski, 1925–2004. And Zdenkica Defrančeski, 1943–1945 — a child of two, buried in Zagreb in the last year of the war. The Croatian spelling of this surname is not a scribal accident and it is not only in the newspapers: there are people under stones with it.

rows.lab: The oldest date in the whole sweep is in Dalmatia
rows.text: Gioannes Maria De Franceschi, born 1581, died 20 March 1645, buried at Omiš. Then Mandalina, baptised 14 November 1634; Nicolaa, 12 January 1644; Francesco, 1 August 1657; and Nicolo, born 1626, buried at Split on 18 May 1716 at ninety. A Dalmatian line of the name running from the year the Venetians finished the walls of Omiš to the eighteenth century, and no connection to Istria has been shown.

rows.lab: And Fiume is older than anything in Istria
rows.text: Francischina, 7 November 1620. Catterina, 15 November 1621. Franciscu, 23 February 1625. Joannem Antonio, 6 September 1626. Gioanna Victoria, 19 April 1628. Maria, 9 September 1632. Zuane, 13 April 1632. The clerk writes «de Francesco» in the 1620s and «de Franceschi» by the later 1620s — the surname settling into its form inside one register.

rows.lab: What the sweep does not settle
rows.text: Bakar does not appear here, because the town groups were built before the Bakar correction and Bakar was not one of them; the separate Bakar query stands at twelve people over three generations and is published on its own page. Gologorica returns one record and Gračišće none — not because the family was not there, which the parish books prove it was, but because those registers are not in this index. An index sweep measures what has been indexed. It is a map of the record, not of the people.

resweep.method2: Six spellings — De Franceschi, Defranceschi, Defranceski, De Franceski, Defrančeski, Franceschi — each run against five country filters, thirty jobs in all, each paged to the index's own ceiling of about 1,400. Every record was matched whole, as JSON, against thirty-six place patterns, rather than against a short extracted summary string. That is the fix. The earlier method matched a truncated field and therefore missed most of what was there.

filter.heading: The place parameter does not filter. Tested, and it does not.
filter.lead: On 9 September 2026 this archive tested the search endpoint its own sweep is built on. The result changes how every place-based number here should be read.

rows.text:
The same query was run against FamilySearch's persona search with the place parameter set to **Vižinada**, **Draguč**, **Dubrovnik**, **Vodnjan**, **Rovinj**, **Gračišće**, **Kaštelir**, **Ližnjan**, and to **«Zzzznowhere»** and **«Atlantis»**.

**Every single one returned the same total: 3,652.**

`q.anyPlace` is a **relevance boost, not a filter**. It changes the order of the results and nothing else. A place it does not recognise is silently ignored and you get the whole set back, with no error and no warning.

rows.lab: And two real villages come back identical
rows.text:
**Vižinada** and **Draguč** return the *same records, in the same order*. They cannot be told apart by this route at all. **Dubrovnik** returns exactly what no place parameter returns — the unfiltered head of the list.

`f.recordPlace` *is* a genuine filter, but it rejects plain town names: `Vodnjan`, `Rovinj` and a numeric place id all return **0**, and a name with spaces is refused outright — «Filter value for term=record_place must not contain whitespace». **No working place filter was found on this endpoint.**

rows.lab: What this does, and does not, invalidate
rows.text:
**It does not invalidate the sweep's positive counts.** The method here already compensated: for each place the top hundred were pulled and **kept only if the record's own place text actually named that town**. That check is what makes the numbers above mean anything, and it is why they were published as *weight, not population*.

**It does sharpen the blanks.** Thirty-nine places returned nothing, and this page already said a blank proves nothing because those registers are browse-only and unindexed. There is now a **second** reason: the search can only ever see what ranks into the top hundred of a re-ranked list of 3,652 records. A blank is a statement about ranking, not about a province.

**And it retires a queue item.** This archive was carrying «Vižinada — 53 records, unread». Those records are on **DGS 005497893**, which is the **Vodnjan** baptism film, and they have now been read: they are the eight Vodnjan households. The item was a ghost of the two-parish reel.

**Resolve each record to the film it sits on, then ask the catalogue what that film is.** That is what produced this archive's ninety-three-parish list, and it is what found Vodnjan.

With one caution learned the same day: **a film can carry more than one parish**, and the catalogue answers a film-number query with the first creator on the reel. Resolve to the film, then read the item list — not the film heading. *(doc — every claim on this page was produced by running the queries and is reproducible)*

filter.source_filter: FamilySearch persona search endpoint, tested 9 September 2026 against ten place values including two nonsense controls.
